CLINICAL HISTORY
Diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma
Specimen Type: Breast biopsy tissue sections
Clinical Question: HER2 status assessment for treatment planning

TEST PERFORMED
HER2 (ERBB2) Gene Amplification by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using the GenProbe XR-2000 ERBB2/SE17 dual probe system on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded breast biopsy tissue sections. The ERBB2 probe targets the HER2 gene at 17q12 (spectrum orange) and the SE17 probe targets the chromosome 17 centromere (spectrum green). Analysis was performed on two tissue blocks with correlation to HER2 immunohistochemistry.

RESULTS

BLOCK A1 ANALYSIS
Cells counted: 90
Mean HER2 copy number per cell: 3.50
Mean chromosome 17 centromere per cell: 2.69
HER2/Chr17 ratio: 1.30
Interpretation: NEGATIVE for HER2 gene amplification

BLOCK A2 ANALYSIS
Cells counted: 130
Mean HER2 copy number per cell: 5.30
Mean chromosome 17 centromere per cell: 3.84
HER2/Chr17 ratio: 1.38
Interpretation: NEGATIVE by ratio criteria; EQUIVOCAL by absolute HER2 copy number

INTERPRETATION
Block A1 demonstrates no evidence of HER2 gene amplification with a HER2/Chr17 ratio <2.0 and mean HER2 copy number <6.0 per cell.

Block A2 shows a HER2/Chr17 ratio <2.0 (negative by ratio criteria), however the mean HER2 copy number of 5.30 falls within the equivocal range (≥4.0 to <6.0 signals/cell) according to ASCO/CAP 2018 guidelines. The increased chromosome 17 centromere count (3.84) suggests possible chromosome 17 polysomy.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
HER2 gene amplification status is a critical biomarker for breast cancer treatment decisions. HER2-positive tumors may benefit from HER2-targeted therapies such as trastuzumab, pertuzumab, or T-DM1. The findings in this case indicate:
- Block A1: HER2-negative status
- Block A2: Borderline negative/equivocal status requiring careful clinical correlation

RECOMMENDATIONS
Results interpreted according to 2018 ASCO/CAP HER2 testing guidelines for breast cancer. Given the equivocal findings in Block A2, correlation with HER2 immunohistochemistry results is recommended. If IHC shows 2+ staining, consideration may be given to repeat testing on an alternative specimen or alternative HER2 testing methodology. Clinical management decisions should incorporate all available pathologic and clinical data.

Electronically signed by: Dr. [redacted name], Board Certified Molecular Pathologist
Date: [redacted date]
